title: Provenance absence claims require source-class coverage

observed: The queue requires locating an originating decision log, language lexicon, project document, or authorized history source for M-004, M-005, and M-006.
Repository connector search and recent-commit inspection provide bounded repository evidence, not exhaustive coverage of every ref or every source class.
inferred: An undifferentiated not-found result can create a false global absence claim.
Exhausting repository history cannot establish absence from non-repository source classes.
proposed: Track coverage independently for repository_refs, reachable_commits, decision_logs, language_lexicons, project_documents, authorized_history, and file_archive.
Permit unlocated_after_declared_coverage only when every required accessible source class has an explicit coverage disposition.
For restricted sources, retain a minimal attestation rather than source contents.
superseded: Treating repository search silence as proof that an identifier never existed.
Treating source classes as if they have identical accessibility and publication boundaries.
unresolved: No immutable accepted origin has been located for M-004, M-005, or M-006.
Exhaustive accessible-ref and reachable-commit traversal has not been demonstrated in this run.
Coverage of decision logs, language lexicons, project documents, authorized history, and file archives remains independently unproven.

source_coverage_contract.fail_closed_rule: Every absence statement must name the source classes and coverage horizon it establishes; global absence claims are prohibited.

falsification_routes: Produce an immutable public source explicitly assigning a disputed identifier with matching namespace, owner, semantic role, and temporal precedence.
Produce an authorized minimal attestation satisfying the required fields for a restricted source assignment.
Demonstrate that a declared exhaustive source-class inventory omitted an accessible object, returning that class to incomplete coverage.
